WEAK_RESULTS_PUBLISHED_RATHER_THAN_HIDDE: (1) The harness is NOT AN INSTRUMENT below a few microseconds: it perturbs a 1.9 us payload by a median factor of 3.515 over five trials, and the product says so where the figure is quoted rather than reporting the duration. (2) The perturbation ratio is noise-limited at the top of the range - the min over five trials is 0.962 at 153 us and 0.982 at 300 us, BELOW 1.0, which is a shared two-core host descheduling the measuring process; the outliers are left in the published table with the reason rather than trimmed. (3) The tamper seal is NOT A SECURITY BOUNDARY: a per-process module-private key, forgeable by same-process code, and no design in Python can prevent that. (4) mint() lets its caller choose a provenance, so a false claim AT THE SOURCE is possible; the guarantee is only that a provenance once claimed cannot be strengthened, laundered or lost. (5) A PlatformAttestation can be hand-built with matches_target true. (6) Dependency ranges measured at ONE version each except ruff: numpy>=2.5,<2.6 measured only at 2.5.3 while 2.5.4 exists on PyPI and is admitted by the ceiling, untested because installing a second numpy would need pip against a shared pre-pinned interpreter. (7) Hypothesis found numpy.mean returning inf for a REPRESENTABLE mean at [8.988465674311579e+307, 8.98846567431158e+307] because it sums before dividing, and numpy.std is worse because it squares; all aggregates now compute in longdouble and non-representable results are refused by name rather than reported as inf.
